title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## CW-WAM Force-Sensitive Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
CW‑WAM introduces a unified world‑action model that predicts video, motion, and contact wrench jointly; by feeding the predicted wrench into a 20 Hz admittance controller it lifts square‑peg insertion success from 25 % to 70 % and power‑adapter insertion from 40 % to 95 %, while halving force‑tracking RMSE from 4.8 N to 2.7 N.

### The Caveats
The gains are reported only against a single “WAM‑without‑wrench” baseline, so superiority over stronger manipulation models is unproven.

## Digit Humanoid Robots at AGCO Kansas Plant

### The Breakthrough
AGCO will pilot Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid in its Hesston, Kansas factory from 2027, using the cloud‑based Arc platform to manage fleets that sort, stack parts and move storage totes, leveraging over 65 000 hours of real‑world operation.

### The Caveats
No performance metrics, baseline comparisons, or cost‑scalability data are provided, leaving claimed safety and productivity gains unverified.

## Nvidia DSX Pods & Agile One SN Humanoid

### The Breakthrough
Nvidia’s DSX Pods pack the DSX reference architecture into a transportable container with 800 V DC power and 17 km of Spectrum‑X cabling, promising datacenter rollout in about a month; the Agile One SN humanoid offers a 1.4 m body, five‑finger tactile hands and 2 070 FP4 TFLOPS compute as a ready‑to‑use research platform.

### The Caveats
The announcement lacks independent performance data or real‑world trials for either the pods or the humanoid robot.

## RISE Test‑Time Motion Steering

### The Breakthrough
RISE learns a vocabulary of fall‑recovery primitives and a visual diffusion planner that, when biased with task‑specific costs at inference, steers a Unitree G1 robot toward desired headings or speeds, enabling on‑the‑fly selection among diverse recovery motions without additional training.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no quantitative comparison to existing fall‑recovery baselines, leaving benefits unsubstantiated.

## Earth‑Trained Humanoid Policies on the Moon

### The Breakthrough
Training with gravity randomization and 3‑D resistive‑force‑theory soil models yields Earth‑trained policies that survive up to 75 % on lunar rigid ground, while rough‑terrain training pushes survival to 0.99 on Moon‑like slopes.

### The Caveats
All results are from simulation of a Unitree G1 with a synthetic soil model; no hardware or real‑lunar testing is presented.

## AtomicRL Long‑Horizon Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
AtomicRL adds Semantic‑Aware Policy Optimization and Bottleneck‑Adaptive Target Exploration to VLA policies, improving LIBERO‑LONG scores by 3.6‑4 % over PPO and boosting CALVIN ABC‑D full‑task scores up to 9.5 %, with a 21.3 % average gain in real‑world deployments.

### The Caveats
Improvements are shown only against a single PPO baseline, so superiority over stronger current RL methods remains unclear.

## MuTRAP Backdoor & PROTEA Safety Monitor

### The Breakthrough
The MuTRAP backdoor embeds a two‑letter trigger “CF” that forces an LLM planner to replace a benign “cut apple” step with “cut hand”; PROTEA mitigates this by sequentially evaluating each planned action, achieving reasonably accurate detection of malicious plans in the demonstrated setup.

### The Caveats
The safety monitor is demonstrated on a single lab robot with no baseline comparison to existing safety frameworks.

## Lucid Bolt Robotaxi Fleet with Nvidia Alpamayo

### The Breakthrough
Lucid will equip at least 25 000 Bolt robotaxis in Europe with Nvidia’s Alpamayo self‑driving stack, running on the Hyperion compute‑sensor reference design and Halos safety suite, starting with a data‑collection program in Madrid in 2027.

### The Caveats
The claim lacks independent verification, performance data, or safety validation for the proposed rollout.

## Drake Model‑Based Design Toolkit

### The Breakthrough
Drake is an open‑source C++/Python library that unifies high‑fidelity continuous dynamics, trajectory optimization, contact modeling and system‑level simulation, providing built‑in solvers for planning and control across manipulators to legged robots.

### The Caveats
The repository offers no empirical benchmarks or hardware experiments to substantiate its broad applicability claims.

### Priority
CW‑WAM offers a concrete, quantitative advance in force‑sensitive manipulation that directly translates to higher success rates on real‑world assembly tasks, making it the most actionable development for robotics engineers right now.

### One action
Integrate CW‑WAM’s contact‑wrench prediction module into your next insertion or assembly pipeline.

### What to watch
Upcoming work in manipulation spans three angles: CW‑WAM focuses on vision‑driven wrench prediction for precise force control; AtomicRL tackles long‑horizon task sequencing via reinforcement learning; and RISE addresses rapid adaptation for fall recovery. Watching how these approaches converge—especially any cross‑integration of force‑aware models with RL‑driven policies—will reveal the next wave of robust, adaptable robot skill learning.
